missing_supported_requirements.reason: Draft is generic policy text and does not disclose the actual metrics required by applicable IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards for each material sustainability-related risk/opportunity (no entity-specific metric list or values). Coverage matrix indicates only partial support.

Draft does not disclose the actual metrics the entity uses to measure/monitor each sustainability-related risk or opportunity (entity-specific metrics not presented). Coverage matrix indicates only partial support.

Draft states a requirement to label/define metrics clearly, but does not actually provide meaningful, clear and precise labels/definitions for the entity’s disclosed metrics/targets (no entity-specific metric naming/definitions shown). Coverage matrix indicates partial support.

Draft describes what to do if a metric is redefined/replaced, but does not provide an entity-specific explanation of changes to any redefined/replaced metric in the reporting period. Coverage matrix indicates partial support.
Draft does not provide entity-specific reasons for any metric redefinition/replacement (including why it provides more useful information). Coverage matrix indicates partial support.

required_fixes: Replace generic policy-style statements with entity-specific disclosures: list the actual metrics used (and, where applicable, required by IFRS SDS) for each sustainability-related risk/opportunity, including the metric values for the reporting period as applicable.
Provide entity-specific metric/target labels and definitions (clear names, what is measured, units, boundaries/scope).

If any metrics were redefined/replaced, add the entity-specific explanation of what changed and why (including why the new/redefined metric is more useful); if none were changed, remove or tailor the boilerplate so it does not imply changes occurred.
ifrs_coverage_judge.summary: The section largely restates IFRS S1/S2 requirements in boilerplate form rather than providing entity-specific metrics, targets, definitions, and (where relevant) explanations of metric changes. Several requirements flagged as only partially supported in the coverage matrix remain unfulfilled in the draft. No invented 'missing data' statements were found.

questionable_claims.claim_text: Phrasing throughout implies the entity actually performs these disclosures (e.g., “The entity discloses…”, “Metrics disclosed include…”, “are applied consistently over time”).
questionable_claims.why_questionable: The draft reads like a statement of what the entity does, but it provides no entity-specific metrics/targets, sources, calculations, or comparative restatements to substantiate that these disclosures have in fact been made. As written, it is safer as a requirements/policy description rather than an assertion of completed disclosure.

required_fixes: Clarify the section’s intent: either (a) explicitly label it as a summary of IFRS S1 disclosure requirements / reporting policy (e.g., “We will disclose…” / “We are required to disclose…”), or (b) add entity-specific disclosures (actual metrics, targets, sources, calculation methods, third-party validators, performance vs targets, revisions, and comparatives) to support the “The entity discloses…” wording.

If keeping assertive language (“are applied consistently over time”), add evidence in the report (e.g., prior-year comparatives, restatement notes, or a statement that no redefinitions/revisions occurred) to avoid implying unsubstantiated historical consistency.
evidence_judge.summary: No concrete factual metrics/targets are asserted; the content largely restates IFRS S1-style disclosure requirements. The main risk is interpretive: the repeated “The entity discloses…” wording can be read as claiming the entity has provided these disclosures, without including the underlying entity-specific data in this section.

voice_issues: Section is written entirely in generic third-person ('the entity') and reads as a standard summary rather than as disclosure by a specific reporting entity; style guide prefers first-person plural for the entity’s own actions.
Voice is requirements-recital rather than decision-useful disclosure about how the entity actually measures, calculates, and reports its metrics and targets.
structure_issues: Subsections do not start with a one-sentence purpose statement explaining what follows and why it matters; bullets begin immediately after headings.
There is no initial overview paragraph for the Metrics and Targets pillar explaining scope, linkage to IFRS S1 vs S2, and how the metrics support assessment of prospects.
The section does not clearly separate general sustainability metrics (IFRS S1) from climate-specific metrics (IFRS S2).
No closing connectivity sentences are provided to link this section to related sections or financial statements.
The content is entirely narrative and bullet-based; there is no metrics register table or structured tabular presentation, even though tables are specified as the primary disclosure vehicle.
Principles ('what') and mechanics ('how') are not clearly separated; for example, metric selection, boundaries, data collection, and estimation methodologies are not described as distinct blocks.
No data currency or update cadence statement is included before where tables/metrics would appear.
wording_issues: Language is heavily templated and requirement-like (e.g., 'The entity discloses...') rather than entity-specific disclosure using preferred verbs such as 'define', 'measure', 'calculate', 'report', and 'reconcile'.

Sentences are generally clear and short, but they lack explicit definitional constructions for metrics (e.g., 'Metric is defined as...') and do not distinguish between current-period facts, estimates, and forward-looking intentions.

The section does not use explicit status labels for applicability or availability (e.g., 'not applicable', 'not reported for the period', 'under development') where missing or incomplete data would be expected.
Forward-looking aspects (targets, revisions, improvements) are described generically without cautious modality (e.g., 'may', 'could', 'is expected to').
Some bullets combine multiple ideas (e.g., performance plus progress plus legal targets) rather than using tightly parallel, single-idea phrasing.
table_figure_issues: No tables or figures are included, despite the style guide specifying a metrics register table as the primary disclosure vehicle for this section.
Because there are no tables or figures, there are no captions, numbering, or cross-references, which are required for traceability and PDF layout alignment.
No space is reserved or signposted for assurance legends, boundary notes, or methodology footnotes that would normally accompany metrics tables.
required_fixes: Add an opening overview paragraph for the Metrics and Targets section that explains the purpose of the disclosures, how they support assessment of sustainability-related risks and opportunities, and how they relate to IFRS S1 and IFRS S2.

Introduce each subsection (Identification and sourcing of metrics, Entity-developed metrics, Targets, Consistency and comparability, Labelling and definitions) with a one-sentence purpose statement before listing bullets.

Recast the voice to align with the report’s chosen point of view: use first-person plural ('we') for the entity’s own processes and metrics, and third-person or passive voice only when describing externally defined IFRS requirements.
Explicitly distinguish between general sustainability metrics (IFRS S1) and climate-related metrics (IFRS S2), either via subheadings or clear narrative separation.

Insert a methodology and boundary paragraph covering metric selection criteria, reporting boundaries, data sources, estimation approaches, and treatment of changes over time, using preferred verbs such as 'define', 'measure', 'calculate', 'estimate', and 'validate'.

Develop and reference a structured metrics register table (or tables) that includes, at minimum, columns for metric name, definition, boundary, reporting-period value/status, source type, internal source reference, mapping to report pillar/section, and assurance status; number and caption the table(s) and reference them in the narrative.

Add explicit language and placeholders for handling missing or incomplete data (e.g., 'not reported for the period', 'under development'), including brief reason categories and planned improvement directions, in line with the missing data protocol.
Refine bullets to ensure single-idea, parallel phrasing and to incorporate definitional wording where appropriate (e.g., 'Definition', 'Type of measure', 'Calculation method', 'Limitations').
Include a short data currency and update cadence statement (e.g., reporting period, frequency of updates, and where updated metrics are presented) before the metrics tables.

Close the section, or each major subsection, with a brief connectivity sentence linking metrics and targets to related governance, strategy, risk management sections and to relevant financial statement areas using generic cross-reference placeholders.
style_judge.summary: The section is broadly aligned with IFRS-style content and uses a neutral, formal tone, but it reads as a generic requirements summary rather than an audit-ready, entity-specific Metrics and Targets disclosure. It lacks the required overview and purpose statements, does not separate IFRS S1 and S2 metrics, omits the metrics register tables that should be the primary disclosure vehicle, and does not implement the missing data protocol or connectivity statements. With structural enhancements, clearer entity-focused wording, and the addition of tables and methodology detail, it can be brought into full compliance with the approved authoring style.
